design:
## Design tests

The refined visuals and the new placement rules were then read blind in six whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v016.md`), each of the three v0.15 failures put back among the kind of neighbours that had pulled its reading away. The stalking cat read as stalking beside a child reaching for a ball in the tree ("creeps along toward a blue bird ... so the cat looks like it is stalking the bird and might pounce"), the stuck girl as stuck in two busy playgrounds ("Because his end stays down, she seems to be stuck up in the air"), and a bird on a garden fence with a clothesline as perched on the fence, not the line. The sleeping baby, the shower of water, the lower catch, the dog clear of the knob and the dog on its lead walking ahead read as intended.

Two remarks there led to changes before the set was built: the pram's cream oval of a blanket was still "a flat disc or lid sitting on top" (it became the pink quilt), and a child jumping under the washing line was "perhaps ... grab[bing] the clothes" (a jumper is now kept from the line).
intro: All three templates that failed the v0.15 gate pass the thirteenth screen: the stalking cat read as stalking in all four of its pictures, three of them crowded tier-4 pictures ("creeping along the top of the fence toward the bird ... as if about to pounce"); the girl on the seesaw as stuck in all three, the set picture a busy playground again ("the man doesn't seem to notice she can't get down"); and every perched bird as perched where it was. For the second screen running no item was misread, set or probes, and 743 of 746 scored items had full marks. The set scored 0.996 over all items (0.988 in v0.15), its inferences 0.99, the highest of any screen, with 1.1 unintended oddities per picture (1.4). 63 of 64 templates pass the gate; the one that falls short, the photographer, lost half a point in a single probe that put him in a park with nobody to photograph, where he "holds binoculars or a camera up to his face".
screen: Across all 64 pictures only 3 of 746 scored items fell short of full marks (7 of 738 in v0.15) and none was misread: in the set, a stalking cat on the ground whose crouch read as "leaping/running toward" the bird ("as if about to pounce" was right) and a duck whose motion lines "could mean it is swimming quickly toward the food, or just that it is moving"; in the probes, the photographer with binoculars or a camera. Unintended oddities fell from 29 to 23 in the set and from 39 to 37 in the probes. None of the v0.15 oddities came back as reported then: no one at the back of the playground looks too big, no door knob sits on a dog's head, no figure stands over another's feet, no walker or ball heads for another event's objects, no jumper seems to float, no water reads as blobs, and every baby in a pram has a sleeping face. What remains is small: drops above the sprinkler's box that "could be water coming out of the box", a bird on the playground railing read "on top of the slide" in front of it, things at the same depth that touch (a man's feet at the back edge of a bench), a goat taken for a lamb, and runners with "no visible reason".
redrawn: The three failures pass: the stalking cat at 0.96 over four pictures, the stuck girl and the perched bird at 1.00. The visuals refined for the v0.15 oddities read with full marks wherever they were screened: the star jump in all three of its pictures, the watering can's shower and the frying pan's pour, the sleeping baby in the pram, the lower catch, the dog by the door, the open-eyed readers, the low kick and the square-wheeled bicycle.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (52 in three, 7 in four, 3 in five, 2 in six). One fails, on a single hedge in a probe and no misread: the photographer (0.83), read in full in its two other pictures. The v0.17 fix: a camera that cannot be taken for binoculars, and a photographer placed only with someone or something to photograph.
